solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aces?

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the receiver cannot even get a racket to, so the rally ends at once

explanation.surface: A one-word query about top cards or star pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: Aces suggests cards or pilots; the tennis sense, a serve that goes unanswered, is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace wins a point the opponent never sends back, so each is literally a point that is not returned.

clue.text: See our pie range, including beef for druggie

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the meat word into their middle
to range is to wander about, so the letters of our pie roam into a new order

parts.note: beef is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: Look at our selection of pies, one of them steak-filled, if you are hooked on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is the anagram signal and 'including' the container. 'See' is a link. De Quincey's Confessions made the term famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual taker of the poppy-derived narcotic is a classic Victorian term for an addict, a drug user.

clue.text: Accepting hollow defence in any case is criminal (what does it every time!)

indicators.note: the phrase in any case takes in the two remaining letters before being scrambled
criminal in the sense of wrong or crooked, so the letters are set out in a new order
hollow means the word defence is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer notes that a defendant who took up a flimsy defence is a crook either way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties DEFENCE to DE, 'Accepting' puts it in IN ANY CASE, and 'criminal' rearranges the lot. The definition leans on the Sinatra lyric 'Nice and easy does it every time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song line says that a gentle unhurried approach always succeeds, so the phrase is what does the trick.

clue.text: Eleven years older, very badly lacking energy, he doesn't want return in court

definitions.text: he doesn't want return in court

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the phrase plus the added letter are jumbled
lacking means one letter is taken away from the jumbled letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone now over a decade older, and in very poor shape, seems to be avoiding something in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ELEVEN YEARS OLDER plus V are rearranged ('badly') and one E goes ('lacking energy'). Court here is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player of this style rushes the net after serving to volley, aiming to end the point without a long baseline rally.

clue.text: Freddie's not leaving without the urn: he has bowl — and unusual successes!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes round the trophy
not cancels the following word, so its letters are removed from the cricketer's surname

parts.note: Freddie is the nickname of the England cricketer Andrew Flintoff
leaving means going off
the Ashes, the England-Australia cricket trophy, is a small urn
taken as written
a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel

explanation.surface: Cricketer Freddie Flintoff stays on without the Ashes trophy, takes the ball, and enjoys rare triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leaving' strips the second half of the surname, and 'without' means outside. Flintoff was an England cricketer; the Ashes, the England-Australia cricket trophy, is kept in a tiny urn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for brief successes that are not repeated, so they are rare, one-off triumphs.

clue.text: Pub commotion interrupts beloved visionary writer

parts.note: jo is an old Scots word for a sweetheart

indicators.note: interrupts means the first pair of pieces breaks into the middle of the other pair

parts.note: a seer is someone who has visions of the future
PH is the abbreviation for public house
hell, as in raising hell, is an uproar

explanation.surface: A row in a pub breaks up a much-loved, inspired author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' splits the visionary piece just before its last two letters. The author wrote Catch-22.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist who wrote Catch-22 is a famous author.

clue.text: Bird dressing for a pantomime

indicators.note: dressing means the bird is wrapped round the other letters like clothing

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
per means for, as in so much per head

explanation.surface: A feathered costume is wanted for a Christmas pantomime show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' and 'pantomime' look like a costume for a show; 'for a' reads as a Latin-style rate word plus A, with 'dressing' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime in the sense of silly clowning or horseplay is jesting, playful foolery.

clue.text: Runner, not quite at full pelt?

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: the full pelt of an animal is its whole skin

explanation.surface: Someone running, but not quite flat out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'at full pelt' suggests speed; pelt is an animal hide, SKIN, cut short. A runner here is something that slides along snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner can be a long narrow blade that slides, such as a sledge runner, which describes a snow board for each foot.

clue.text: See 15
I say, with pretence, "fine chopper!"

definitions.meaning: one who minces words or speaks with an affected, prissy manner, saying things like I say
a kitchen machine that chops meat finely

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is a person speaking or walking affectedly; the other is a kitchen gadget that grinds meat small.

clue.text: Peppered back of setter during out-of-control rave-up

indicators.note: during means the turned name is set inside the jumbled letters
out of control signals that the letters of the party word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, letters RAVEUP

indicators.note: back of means the setter's name is read from the back

parts.note: Io is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: Seasoning gets into the act at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of setter' turns the setter's pseudonym around, and 'during' sets it inside the anagram ('out-of-control') of the party word, AUPVRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term means cooked with crushed peppercorns, as in steak with a pepper crust.

clue.text: Book a series of requiem masses

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A book containing a set of masses for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel of a matchmaking heroine is a well-known book title.

clue.text: Spiritually, the very following envisaged for openers

indicators.note: following places the remaining pieces after the opening letter
for openers means to begin with, so only the start of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written
really means very, as in really good

explanation.surface: In a religious sense, the very next thing is pictured for starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for openers' takes the first letter of 'envisaged', and 'following' places the other pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is airy and heavenly is done in an otherworldly, spiritual way.

clue.text: Finally traps French toreador's target, heading back very quickly

indicators.note: traps means the phrase for finally holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: at last means finally

indicators.note: heading back means the first letter of the word is moved to the end

parts.note: a bullfighter's target is the bull

explanation.surface: A bullfighter's quarry is finally cornered and turns for home at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading back' sends the first letter of the bull to its end, and 'traps' sets French plus that inside the two words for finally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at maximum power or speed, so it describes moving very fast.

clue.text: Sawyer's mate finally runs through board's conclusion

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the friend's name, which runs through the lodging word

parts.note: Huckleberry Finn is the friend of Tom Sawyer in Mark Twain
digs is informal British for lodgings, board and lodging

explanation.surface: Tom Sawyer's pal finally sprints through a committee's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The last N of FINN 'runs through' DIGS, giving FIN + DINGS. Digs is British slang for rented lodgings. The definition is singular in sense: a board's findings are its conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The results an inquiry reaches after investigation are its verdict or conclusion.

clue.text: Palestinian's fairly battle-worn condition

indicators.note: battle-worn suggests something knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain letters, giving the word with its final s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Palestinian is in a fairly war-weary state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle-worn' rearranges PALESTINIANS + FAIRLY into the two words. It is an old name for polio.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for poliomyelitis, a viral disease, which is a medical condition.

clue.text: Fixed quick

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is firmly secured, as with colours that do not run; the other is speedy.

clue.text: See 4
On holiday with a top man in Mercia

parts.note: off means away from work, as in a day off

explanation.surface: Travelling on vacation with a leading figure in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; its greatest king built a famous dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth-century king of Mercia, builder of the earthwork on the Welsh border, was its ruler.

clue.text: Analysed sample on nasty new growth

indicators.note: analysed means broken down into parts, so the letters are separated and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A lab tests a specimen taken from an unpleasant lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Analysed' rearranges SAMPLE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumour, a mass of abnormal tissue, is a new growth in the body.

clue.text: Rather foolhardy, and a little streaky?

definitions.meaning: a thin slice of streaky bacon

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of reckless; the other is a single slice of bacon, streaky being a fatty British cut.

clue.text: Artist with cycling crusade

parts.note: and means with, as in fish and chips

indicators.note: cycling means letters are taken from one end of the word and put on the other

parts.note: a crusade is a holy war

explanation.surface: A painter goes on a bicycle campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves HOL from the front of HOLYWAR to the end, giving YWARHOL.
explanation.definitionFit: The American pop artist known for soup cans and Marilyn prints is a famous artist.

clue.text: Stand at funeral to speak about porter?

indicators.note: to speak about signals the word for porter is said out loud

parts.note: porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A mourner asks whether to say something about the doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a person; here it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame on which a coffin rests before burial is a stand used at funerals.

clue.text: See 2
Speedy measure: Hamilton on pole gets through motor racing circuit, breaking old record

indicators.note: breaking means the other pieces burst into the middle of the record

parts.note: LP, a long-playing vinyl record, is old technology
Indy is short for IndyCar racing in America

indicators.note: on pole means at the front of the grid, so the first letter of the driver is used

parts.note: a circle, the letter O, is a circuit

explanation.surface: Lewis Hamilton starts at the front, laps the track and smashes an old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on pole' takes the front letter of Hamilton, the F1 driver, and 'breaking' puts the pieces inside the vinyl record. Measure is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an old word for a dance, and this energetic swing dance is fast.

clue.text: Pulse the stableman's raised

indicators.note: raised means read upwards, which in a down entry turns the word around

parts.note: a lad is a stable worker who looks after racehorses

explanation.surface: The stable worker's heart rate has gone up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse suggests heartbeat; it is a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds like lentils, and the Indian lentil dish is one.

clue.text: Orient going through years of upheaval

indicators.note: going through means the compass word passes into the middle of the two letters

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, doubled for years
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: The Far East has been through years of turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: Years gives YY, two year abbreviations, with EAST 'going through' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Frothy and fermenting, the adjective is used figuratively for times that are restless and turbulent.
